title: Connected Vehicle Edge Inference — Engagement Outline & Pricing Sketch
body:
Executive summary:

This note captures a proposed engagement for AutonomyOne to evaluate Redwood Inference running optimized language-model inferencing at the vehicle gateway. Goal: enable a fleet-level diagnostic & driver-assist conversational agent that runs inference on roadside / in-vehicle gateways (intermittent cloud connectivity) and falls back to hosted Redwood when connectivity permits. This is an engagement outline (not final SOW) and includes technical assumptions, workshop agenda, success criteria, and a pricing sketch for discovery -> pilot -> scale phases.

Key differentiators targeted:
- Low-latency on-device/gateway inference (tail latency <120ms for 128-token responses under target load)
- Prefix/KV caching to reduce token compute during repeated diagnostic queries
- Quantized model variants for memory-constrained gateways (4-bit or 6-bit profiles)
- Transparent routing: local gateway first, then dedicated Redwood region fallback

Assumptions (please validate with AutonomyOne before drafting final SOW):
- Target fleet: 2,500 vehicles for pilot; each vehicle has a gateway with 8GB VRAM equivalent (NVIDIA Jetson-class or equivalent).
- Typical query size: 30–120 tokens; 95th percentile session length 200 tokens.
- Intermittent connectivity window: 1–12 minutes per hour depending on area.
- Customer provides anonymized sample telemetry + user query corpus for model tuning and prompt templates.

Scope & deliverables (phased):
1) Discovery & Architecture Workshop (2 weeks)
   - Deliverables: workshop notes, reference architecture (network, routing, failover), integration checklist, acceptance criteria.
   - Activities: 1-day onsite/remote workshop with AutonomyOne edge and platform teams; collection of telemetry schema and sample queries.

2) Pilot — Gateway Inference PoC (8 weeks)
   - Deliverables: gateway runtime container (quantized model), KV/prefix cache integration, simple sync protocol to Redwood for model updates & logs, end-to-end demo app (diagnostic assistant), automated perf benchmark harness.
   - Acceptance tests: latency SLOs under guided load, cache hit improvement >=40% on repeat queries, end-to-end correctness smoke tests with 50 curated prompts.

3) Hardening & Scale Plan (4 weeks)
   - Deliverables: autoscaling guidance for Dedicated capacity, cost-per-token profiling for mixed local/cloud routing, rollout plan for fleet-wide deployment, security checklist (KMS/HSM integration points).

4) Optional: On-prem appliance packaging and runbook (additional quoted work)

Milestone timeline and billing (pricing sketch) — illustrative only:
- Discovery: 2 weeks — fixed fee $18,000 (10% due on start, remainder on workshop delivery)
- Pilot: 8 weeks — fixed fee $72,000 (milestone billing: 20% kickoff, 40% mid-pilot demo, 40% delivery)
- Hardening & Scale: 4 weeks — fixed fee $30,000 (50% start, 50% on delivery)
- Optional on-prem packaging: estimate $45k–90k depending on appliance hardware scope
- Support & run-hours: recommendation is Redwood Dedicated reserved capacity + edge support line: estimated $0.015/token equivalent for hosted fallback plus flat $6k/month engineering retainer during pilot (optional).

Total pilot-phase engagement (discovery + pilot + hardening): approx $120k (one-time professional services) + ongoing infra.

Resource plan (Redwood contribution):
- Solutions engineer (Daniel R. Kim) 0.5 FTE during discovery/pilot 
- Applied ML engineer (Priya Nair) 0.6 FTE for model quantization, perf tuning and benchmark harness
- Infra engineer (Marcus Li) 0.3 FTE to integrate KV cache and sync protocol to Redwood cloud
- Product/PM support (Lena Ortiz) 0.1 FTE for acceptance criteria and demo orchestration

Technical notes / checklist:
- Model family: start with a 7B open checkpoint; produce 4-bit and 6-bit quantized build. Validate perplexity/regression on curated prompts before gateway rollouts.
- KV-cache strategy: prefix caching per vehicle session; eviction policy: LRU with periodic snapshot to cloud for analysis.
- Storage: gateway persistent store (encrypted), optional drop-in integration with vehicle ECU bus for minimal telemetry.
- Failover: local inference preferred; if cloud fallback required, route to Redwood Dedicated region pinned to customer account.
- Telemetry: token-level cost traces, latency histograms, cache hit/miss rates; integrate into Redwood Console dashboards.

Security & compliance: 
- Data residency: gateway inference keeps PII on-device; logs to cloud are sanitized by default.
- Key management: recommend KMS/HSM integration for model signing and secret rotation.
- Regulatory: if customer requires air-gapped deployment, quote on-prem packaging separately.

Workshop agenda (half-day recommended prior to kickoff):
- 0:00–0:15: Introductions, objectives, constraints (customer & Redwood)
- 0:15–0:40: Fleet profile & telemetry review (customer leads)
- 0:40–1:10: Architecture options: gateway-first, hybrid, cloud-only (tradeoffs)
- 1:10–1:40: KV-cache design walkthrough and demo harness plan
- 1:40–2:00: Success criteria, acceptance tests, data & access needs, next steps

Success criteria (example set for pilot acceptance):
- Functional: diagnostic assistant returns correct triage classifications for 85% of curated cases
- Performance: 95th percentile response latency <120ms for local inference under target load; cloud fallback latency <350ms
- Cost: effective token compute per vehicle reduced by >=30% vs baseline (no caching, full cloud)
- Operational: logs and dashboards flowing into Redwood Console; automated alerting on cache miss spikes and latency regressions

Risks and mitigations:
- Hardware variance across gateway SKUs — mitigation: profile smallest 8GB-equivalent and produce model variant targeting that memory envelope.
- Dataset drift on vehicle telemetry — mitigation: weekly sync & retrain cadence + alerting on distributional shift.
- Network blackout scenarios — mitigation: ensure critical assist flows are prioritized; provide degraded-mode prompts.

Next steps (for commercial offer / SOW draft):
1) Confirm dataset access, sample telemetry, and primary customer contact by 2025-11-10.
2) Approve discovery scope and schedule workshop week of 2025-11-17.
3) Post-workshop: Redwood to produce a final SOW with exact milestones, MSA/terms, and updated pricing within 7 business days.

Notes to internal team (quick):
- Need benchmark harness (edge emulator) and quantization recipes repo link before kickoff.
- Coordinate with product-hosted-api for fallback routing plan and billing model for mixed local/cloud usage.

(End of outline)
